title: NIH Summer Internship Program (SIP)
costNote: Paid stipend; check current age and grade rules
description: Summer biomedical research internships in NIH labs alongside leading scientists. NIH has recently changed how high school students apply, so check the current eligibility rules (age and grade) on the NIH training site before applying.

title: Stanford Institutes of Medicine Summer Research Program (SIMR)
costNote: No tuition; participants receive a minimum stipend
description: Eight-week research program where high school juniors and seniors work in Stanford medical labs in areas like immunology, neuroscience, cancer biology, and bioengineering.

title: Stanford Medical Youth Science Program (SMYSP)
description: Free five-week residential program for low-income and first-generation high school juniors from Northern and Central California who are interested in science and medicine.

title: HOSA-Future Health Professionals
costNote: Membership dues through your school chapter
description: Student organization for future health professionals. Members compete in events like medical terminology, clinical skills, and health career exploration, from regional to international levels.

title: Fred Hutch Summer High School Internship Program
description: Paid eight-week research internship for Greater Seattle students entering their senior year. Students learn lab safety and techniques, then spend six weeks in a Fred Hutch research group. No prior research experience is required.

title: teen Mental Health First Aid
costNote: Usually free to students through a participating school
description: Training that teaches high school students how to recognize signs of mental health and substance use challenges in friends and how to connect them with a trusted adult.

title: Red Cross First Aid, CPR & Lifeguard Training
description: Certifications in first aid, CPR/AED, babysitting, and lifeguarding. Useful for summer jobs and a strong foundation for students interested in healthcare.

title: AAMC Students & Applicants Resources
description: Free guidance from the organization behind the MCAT on what it takes to become a doctor, including career exploration, the path through college, and how medical school admissions work.

title: ExploreHealthCareers.org
description: A free guide to more than 100 health careers, from nursing and pharmacy to public health and physical therapy, with education requirements, salaries, and summer program listings.

title: CDC Museum Disease Detective Camp
organization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
description: Free day camp for rising juniors and seniors that introduces public health and epidemiology through outbreak investigations, lab activities, and conversations with CDC scientists.

title: Health Career Explorer Posts (Exploring)
description: Career exploration program for ages 14-20 run with local hospitals, EMS agencies, and health organizations, giving hands-on experience with professionals in the field.

title: USA Brain Bee
costNote: Free or low cost locally; cash prizes at nationals
deadline: Local competitions in winter and early spring
description: The national neuroscience competition for students ages 13-19. Students study the brain, compete at local chapter events, and top finishers advance to the national championship and the International Brain Bee.

title: Rockefeller University Summer Science Research Program (SSRP)
costNote: No program fee; need-based stipends may be available
description: Mentored biomedical research program where high school juniors and seniors (16+) work in teams modeled on a Rockefeller lab, design experiments with scientist-mentors, and present their findings.

title: MSK HOPP Summer Student Program
costNote: Stipend after completing the program; strong science grades expected
description: Eight-week cancer research program in MSK's Human Oncology and Pathogenesis Program. Students learn lab techniques, complete an independent project with a mentor, and present a poster. Students from disadvantaged backgrounds are encouraged to apply.

title: UCSF Summer Student Research Program
costNote: No tuition; check the site for current stipend details
description: About nine weeks of mentored research in UCSF clinics and basic science labs, with workshops, seminars, and a closing research symposium. Prioritizes students from backgrounds underrepresented in science.

title: Fred Hutch Pathways Research Explorers
description: Two-week introduction to cancer research for rising 10th and 11th graders who have completed high school biology, with hands-on lab work, conversations with scientists, and a final project. Focused on students from groups excluded from biomedical careers.

title: Area Health Education Center (AHEC) Health Careers Programs
costNote: Usually free or low cost; varies by state
description: State Area Health Education Centers run health career camps, job shadowing, mentoring, and clinical exposure programs for high school students, with a focus on rural, underserved, and underrepresented communities.
